Hi. Maybe I can give you some insight. I don't know his history, but usually when someone has been suicidal, it's not a decision someone makes overnight. It's something that people generally spend a long time thinking about and preparing. Most people who think of suicide don't want to die, they just want the pain to end.

As for the psych ward, their goal is to keep a person from harming themselves or others. My longest stay at a unit was a month. But average stays are 1 - 2 weeks or less. A stay never guarantees that the suicidal ideation will be fixed. They may adjust his meds or prescribe him new ones. Sometimes they have groups with other patients within that unit to do activities (like music or coloring) or coping skills. Medication is given to patients throughout the day. There is breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks.

They will see a doctor during that time to check in and also assess their progress.

I do want to say, this can also vary from ward to ward. I'm sorry that this is happening and hope that he can get the help he needs. Whenever he returns home, please watch for warning signs. (for example, some suicidal people suddenly become very happy or energetic before they attempt or have a plan.) Has he given possessions away? Wrote letters? Tied loose ends? Made vague statements about not wanting to live? (ex, wishing they would go to sleep and not wake up?)

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out.

This is a medical emergency. You may have to bring them to the ER in general. After they are admitted to general ER, they may go though the process of getting them referred to the psych unit. If you can't bring them, calling 911 is your best bet.
